V2 canManage() grants manage on the VIEW scope

`canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. An admin whose all-groups permission has only the `view` scope therefore passes `canManage()`.

The no-arg `canManage()` is what `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` checks (`auth.groups().requireManage()`, GroupsResource.java:181). A view-only admin can create top-level groups. If the body carries an existing `id`, the endpoint also moves that group to top level (GroupsResource.java:192-199).

`canView()` at line 52 is the call that should use `VIEW, MANAGE`. `canManage()` should use only `MANAGE`, like `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79.

The javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator (lines 72-77) says `canManage()` is true for VIEW or MANAGE. It documents the bug and should change with the fix.

`testViewGroups` never checks that a view-only admin is denied a write, so no test catches this.

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource UUIDs, not group ids

The lambda passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission(...)` and adds the same value to `granted`. In V2 the resource name is the group id: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates it with `resourceStore.create(server, name, ...)` where name is `group.getId()`. The resource's own id is a different generated UUID. `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` correctly adds `resource.getName()`.

Two consequences:
1. `hasPermission(groupId, ...)` runs `resourceStore.findByName(server, <resource UUID>)`, which returns null. It then falls back to the all-groups type resource. With only per-group permissions it returns false, so `granted` stays empty. With an all-groups view-members permission, every group resource passes and `granted` holds UUIDs.
2. `UsersResource` and `BruteForceUsersResource` put this set in `UserModel.GROUPS` and `getUsersCount`. An empty set makes `JpaUserProvider.getUsersCount(..., groupIds)` return 0 (JpaUserProvider.java:600, 635, 683). A set of UUIDs matches no group membership.

So `GET /users/count` returns 0 for a group-scoped admin. The search runs unrestricted and `first/max` apply before the per-user `canView` post-filter, so a page can come back short or empty. With an all-groups permission the group-restricted search can return nothing.

The tests do not catch it because they have one user and one page.

Fix: use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission check and the returned set, or make `hasPermission` take the `Resource`.

Javadoc on the new interface is wrong in places

- `requireManageMembers` (lines 132-135) says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false. The implementations check `canManageMembers(group)` (GroupPermissions.java:376-380).
- `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` (lines 142-147) says `@return Stream of IDs` but returns `Set<String>`.
- The `canManage()` doc (lines 72-77) says VIEW grants it in V2. That repeats the defect reported in GroupPermissionsV2.java:70.

No negative or pagination coverage for the new V2 group evaluation

`testViewGroups` stops at listing. It never checks that an admin with only `view` on all groups is refused `groups().add(...)`, subGroup, update or role mapping. That check would have caught the `canManage()` problem.

The user-search tests use a single member and a single page. There is no test of `users().count()`, or of `first`/`max` with several users where only some are in the permitted group. Those are the paths that use `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`.

Multiple real crypto providers on the classpath no longer fail; ties silently resolve by classpath order

The old code threw when more than one CryptoProvider was found. Now the list is sorted by order() and the first one wins, and the ignored ones are logged only at debug level (lines 64-70). DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200, so a classpath that mixes two of them (for example default and FIPS) is no longer rejected. sorted() is stable, so the winner depends on ServiceLoader/classpath order. In a FIPS deployment that could silently pick the non-FIPS provider. The goal is for the 100-order authz provider to lose to a real one. Consider giving the three real providers distinct orders, or keeping the exception when the top two orders are equal. Also, `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a built string as the format string; use `debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` or `debug(...)`.

Dead encoder calls in concatenatedRSToASN1DER

Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances and write the integers, then discard the results. The same values are encoded again at lines 119-120. Remove the two statements.

getBouncyCastleProvider returns the JDK keystore provider

The method returns `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType()).getProvider()`, which is a JDK provider such as SUN, not Bouncy Castle. BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER (common/.../BouncyIntegration.java:34-39) is built from this value, so it becomes the JDK provider name. That is consistent with this provider using only JDK crypto, but the name is misleading. Either add a comment saying so or return null, which BouncyIntegration already handles with a fallback to the first security provider.

Malformed DER can raise unchecked exceptions instead of IOException

readLength() returns -1 for the indefinite-length marker 0x80. readInteger() then calls read(-1), which does `new byte[-1]` and throws NegativeArraySizeException (line 170). A zero-length INTEGER makes `new BigInteger(new byte[0])` throw NumberFormatException (line 73). The decoder's contract is `throws IOException`, and callers that handle only IOException would see a RuntimeException for bad input. Reject a negative length in readInteger/readNext and wrap the empty-integer case in an IOException.

Test uses one default-size EC key for ES256/384/512 and only checks a round trip

`KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` uses the default curve, normally P-256, for all three tests. For ES384 and ES512 the DER signature holds 32-byte r and s values, which are then padded to 48 or 66 bytes, so the test never exercises full-length values for those algorithms. The assertion at line 56 compares rsConcat with rsConcat2, which are both produced by the code under test. An error that is symmetric in the encoder and decoder, or one specific to short or high-bit integers, would pass. Generate a key on the matching curve (secp256r1, secp384r1, secp521r1) per algorithm. Also assert the re-encoded DER against the original JDK signature, or verify the signature with Signature.verify.

Reader thread is never joined and never stopped if a delete fails

The reader thread is started on line 139 and never joined. `deletedAll.set(true)` on line 155 is not in a `finally`. Two problems follow.

1. If any `remove()` on line 153 throws, `deletedAll` is never set. The thread then loops forever, sending requests to the shared admin client, and the test failure surfaces while that thread is still running against the realm that is being torn down.
2. On the passing path, `assertThat` on line 157 runs right after the flag is set. The thread can still be inside a `groups()` call, and any exception from that call lands in `caughtExceptions` after the assertion has already passed. The last read, which is the one that runs after the final delete, is not checked.

Fix: wrap the delete loop in `try/finally` that sets the flag, call `join()` on the thread, then assert. Using an `ExecutorService` or `CompletableFuture` would also work.

Test does not reliably reproduce or pin the race it targets

The reader runs a single `groups(null, 0, MAX, true)` call per iteration, with no coordination with the deletes, so whether a group disappears between listing and `getSubGroupsCount()` is down to timing. The test can pass without the fix. It also does not check which exception was caught, so a failure is reported only as a list of unrelated exceptions. Consider asserting that at least one read ran, and having the reader skip nothing silently. Failing with the first caught exception as the cause would make diagnosis easier. The name `createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti` and the `groupUuuids` typo (three u's) are also worth tidying. Line 117 is a whitespace-only line.

Null-guard added only to getSubGroupsCount; the sibling delegations still NPE for a deleted group

`getSubGroupsCount()` now tolerates `modelSupplier.get()` returning null, which happens when the group was deleted after the adapter was created (`getGroupModel()` at line 299 returns null from `getGroupById`). The three `getSubGroupsStream(...)` overloads at lines 256, 262 and 268 call `modelSupplier.get().…` with no check. A concurrent delete hits them with the same NPE. Decide whether those should also return an empty stream, or document why only the count needs the guard.

The null return is also silent. `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` (services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/utils/GroupUtils.java:90) passes it straight to `setSubGroupCount`, so a group deleted mid-request is still listed, now with a null `subGroupCount`. A missing count is probably acceptable, but it is worth knowing that the response can contain a group that no longer exists.

Removal of unused private method is safe

`groupMatchesSearchOrIsPathElement` was private, and a grep of the repository found no remaining references. The remaining imports are still all used.

Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not compile

`isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` is called with no arguments. The only definition in the repository is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` at UsernamePasswordForm.java:160, and a grep finds no other overload. `UsernameForm` fails to compile, so the `services` module and everything after it fail to build. Pass the user: `context.getUser() != null && !isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`. The intent is to show the form instead of skipping it on re-authentication when passkeys are available.

`user != null` condition removes passkeys from the normal (no user yet) login page

The old code set up WebAuthn (`fillContextForm`) when `context.getUser() == null`, which is the normal first-visit login. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` now returns true only when `user != null`, and both call sites use it (lines 115 and 137). On a normal login the user is null, so `fillContextForm` is no longer called. The login page then has no `//form[@id='webauth']`, no conditional UI and no auto-login with a discoverable key. The same happens after a failed username/password attempt, because `challenge(context, error, field)` runs with the user cleared. The tests in this PR contradict the code. `webauthnLoginWithDiscoverableKey` (PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:83-119) expects auto-login on first open. `passwordLoginWithNonDiscoverableKey` expects the webauth form at line 146 before any user is selected. `webauthnLoginWithExternalKey_reauthentication` expects it after `oauth.openLoginForm()` with no user. The condition probably needs to be `user == null || <re-authentication with passkeys allowed>`, not `user != null`. This also affects `UsernameForm` (via line 47) and `PasswordForm` and `IdpUsernamePasswordForm`, which extend `UsernamePasswordForm`.

reauthenticationOfUserWithoutPasskey disables passkeys at realm level, so it does not test a user without a passkey

The comment at line 277 says passkeys are not enabled for the realm. The comment at line 304 says passkeys should not appear "as this user does not have passkey". The test only sets `setWebAuthnPolicyPasskeysEnabled(Boolean.FALSE)`, so it only covers the realm-disabled case. Nothing tests a passkeys-enabled realm with a re-authenticating user who has no passkey. `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled` does not look at the user's credentials either. The test name and comments describe one behaviour and the test checks another.

Missing @Override on overridden method

`shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators` overrides the method added in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` but has no `@Override`. Add the annotation so the compiler catches a signature drift.

Hung flusher processes are no longer killed: isinstance check never matches a spawn process

The flusher's processes come from `self.mp_context.Process` (line 105), where `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")`. That class is `SpawnProcess`, which subclasses `BaseProcess`. `multiprocessing.Process` is `multiprocessing.context.Process`, the default-context class, and `SpawnProcess` does not inherit from it. I am going from my knowledge of CPython's `multiprocessing/context.py`, not from a file in this repo, so confidence is medium. If that holds, `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is False for every production flusher process.

The old code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally. Now, when `_ensure_processes_alive` detects a `hang`, it skips the kill and starts a replacement process for the same shards (line 259). The hung process stays alive, so two flushers can serve the same shard queues, and one more is leaked on every restart, up to MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS per slot. The `except (ValueError, AttributeError)` cannot help here, because the `isinstance` check skips the call before anything is raised.

The `isinstance` check at line 346 in `join` has the same flaw. That one was already in the base commit, so `terminate()` in `join` was never reached for spawn processes. Use the real type, for example `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)`. Better still, branch on `self.produce_to_pipe is None`.

Redis cluster INFO is queried once per sub-buffer on every submit

Every `SpansBuffer` shares the same Redis client, and `get_memory_info()` returns `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`. That function runs `INFO` against every cluster node (`src/sentry/processing/backpressure/memory.py:82-105`). The loop at lines 300-301 now does this once per flusher process, so there are N identical cluster-wide scans on each `submit`. The `used/available` ratio is the same as before, so the result is correct, just N times the work. Query one buffer only, for example `next(iter(self.buffers.values()))`, or keep a single buffer for memory checks.

`_create_process_for_shard` is dead code

The method has no callers in the diff. Remove it.

Docstring says one process per shard, but processes are capped by max_processes

"Creates one process per shard" contradicts the new behaviour. With `max_processes` set, `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` (line 60). Shards are spread round-robin and share processes. The comment at line 178 ("for all shards handled by this process") is also stale, since it sits above a single `healthy_since` value.

Inconsistent metric tag name and high-cardinality tag value

`wait_produce` is tagged `shards` (line 199). `produce`, `segment_size_bytes` and the unhealthy counter use `shard` (lines 185, 195, 244). The two tag names will split dashboards. The value of `shard` in the first three is a comma-joined list of shards, while `flusher_unhealthy` emits a single shard. The same tag key therefore carries different shapes of value across metrics.

Non-positive --flusher-processes is not validated

`flusher_processes` is a plain `int` click option (`src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:432-437`). A negative value gives a negative `num_processes`, so `range(...)` is empty and `i % self.num_processes` at line 65 yields negative indexes. The result is a KeyError at startup. A value of 0 is silently treated as "unset" by `or` at line 51. Consider `click.IntRange(min=1)`.

`time.sleep(0.1)` is a no-op because the test monkeypatches `time.sleep`

Line 15 does `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)`. That replaces the attribute on the `time` module, so `time.sleep(0.1)` here also does nothing. The added "give flusher threads time" wait therefore gives no time, and it cannot stabilise a race. Capture the real sleep before patching, or poll with a deadline until `messages` is non-empty. The `transaction=True` change in the decorator is not explained anywhere, and neither is the extra `step.poll()`.

New test checks only bookkeeping, not that shared processes flush their shards

`test_flusher_processes_limit` asserts the process count and the total number of shards. It never sends spans, never checks which shards land in which process, and never covers the default (`flusher_processes=None`, one process per shard). It also does not cover the restart path (`_ensure_processes_alive`), which is where the kill bug above sits. A test that flushes spans on shards sharing a process, plus one hang/crash restart test, would cover the new behaviour.

drain_mailbox_parallel deadline (120s) is shorter than its own loop deadline (180s)

`drain_mailbox_parallel` loops until `deadline = timezone.now() + BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET` (line 294). `BATCH_SCHEDULE_OFFSET` is `timedelta(minutes=BACKOFF_INTERVAL)` and `BACKOFF_INTERVAL = 3` (`src/sentry/hybridcloud/models/webhookpayload.py:18`), so the loop is designed to run for up to 180s and only checks the deadline between batches (line 301). The new `processing_deadline_duration=120` is lower than that. With a deep backlog, which is the case the loop exists for, the taskworker will hit the 120s processing deadline mid-loop and fail or retry the task before it ends normally. The 180s cap is then never reached, and the in-flight batch is cut off. `drain_mailbox` (300s) leaves room for 180s plus one delivery, so the two are inconsistent. Set the parallel deadline to at least the 180s loop budget plus one batch of delivery timeouts, e.g. 300 like `drain_mailbox`.

Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with replay event timestamps (likely milliseconds)

`gen_request_data` interleaves errors and recording events with `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"] < event.get("timestamp", 0)`. The error timestamp is the nodestore event `timestamp`, a float in epoch seconds (line 115). The recording event's top-level `timestamp` is an rrweb timestamp. As far as I know rrweb timestamps are epoch milliseconds, but I did not find a conversion in `event_parser.py`. If so, every error compares as earlier than the first event. All errors are then emitted before the first breadcrumb, and the chronological ordering this PR claims is lost. The tests mask this: they use seconds for both (`tests/sentry/replays/test_project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:149,188`) and have one event. Normalize the units before comparing, e.g. convert the error timestamp to ms, and add a test with realistic ms event timestamps and several events.

zip(error_ids, events.values()) pairs ids with results by position

`nodestore.backend.get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id. Its order is not the input order: items fetched from the service come first, then `items.update(cache_items)` appends cached ones (`src/sentry/nodestore/base.py:198-206`). It also deduplicates the ids, and missing ids are omitted. Zipping `error_ids` against `events.values()` can therefore attach the wrong event id to the wrong data. The `id` isn't used in the log text today, but the `ErrorEvent.id` is wrong. Build `node_id -> event_id` and iterate over `events.items()` instead.

Snuba replay query runs even when error context is disabled

`query_replay_instance` and `process_raw_response` run (lines 70-84) before the `enable_error_context=false` check at line 87. When the caller disables error context, the ClickHouse query result is thrown away. Move the query into the `else` branch.

Dead _handle_regex_match left in parametrize_w_experiments

After removing the `ParameterizationRegexExperiment` branch, the local `_handle_regex_match` closure (lines 335-343) is no longer called. The only call was in the deleted `else` branch. Remove it.

age/timestamp exclusivity validators don't enforce what their docstrings say

`validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` only run when their own field is present. A report with neither `age` nor `timestamp` therefore validates, although the docstrings say one must be present. Both are `required=False`, so nothing else enforces it. The checks use truthiness (`initial_data.get("age")`), so `age: 0` together with a `timestamp` passes both validators. The docstring on `validate_timestamp` ("age is absent, but timestamp is present") also reads backwards. Use a `validate()` method that checks `("age" in data) != ("timestamp" in data)`.

Changing the autofix tuning default silently turns off automation for existing projects

`sentry:autofix_automation_tuning` is read with `project.get_option(...)` in `_is_issue_fixable` (`src/sentry/seer/issue_summary.py:253`), and `off` returns False. Projects that never set the option currently resolve to `low`, so the registry default change from `low` to `off` stops automation for all of them without a migration or notice. The same applies to the org default in `constants.py:724`. Is this intended for existing projects, or only for newly created ones? If only for new ones, the default should be applied at project creation (see `set_default_project_autofix_automation_tuning`) rather than by changing the global default.

Analytics event is recorded before the feature-flag check

`analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` check at line 88. Calls from orgs without the feature, which get a 404, are counted as assemble requests. If the event should measure actual usage, record it after the gate.

Flag branch renders an always-empty table

When `use-table-widget-visualization` is on, `TableWidgetVisualization` receives `columns={[]}` and empty `data`, so every table widget renders empty and ignores `result.data` and `result.meta`. The flag is not registered anywhere in the repository (the only match is this line), so it can't be enabled yet. If the flag is later registered before the wiring lands, tables go blank. Either wire the real `columns` and `tableData` from `result`, or leave this branch out until then.

get_environment_info fetches the recommended event for every issue on each merged-PR comment

`issue.get_recommended_event()` runs once per issue in the comment's list comprehension, in both the GitHub and GitLab workflows. Each call reads event data from Snuba and nodestore, serially, on the comment task. A slow call blocks the rest, and the broad `except Exception` only handles errors, not latency. Consider fetching the environments in one query for all issues, or bounding the work.

HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES only applied when a search query is typed

`sortedAndFilteredAttributes` returns `sorted` at line 61-63 when `searchQuery` is empty, so the `!HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(attribute.name)` check at line 67 never runs in the default view. `is_segment`, `project_id` and `received` are therefore shown whenever the search box is empty, and they only disappear once the user types something. Apply the hidden-attribute filter before the empty-query early return, e.g. `const sorted = sortAttributes(attributes).filter(a => !HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES.includes(a.name));`.

Placeholder's right-hand group lost `align-items: center` and `gap`

The removed `FlexBox` styled component set `display:flex; align-items:center; gap: space(1)`. The first replacement group (line 22) keeps `align="center" gap={space(1)}`, but the second group at line 27 is a bare `<Flex>`, so its three 100px placeholders now render with no gap and no vertical centering. The loading skeleton changes visibly. Use `<Flex align="center" gap={space(1)}>` for it too.

Query key no longer includes the organization

The old key was `[path, endpointOptions]`, and the path contained `organization.slug`. The new key is `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]`, and `queryOptions` (built by `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` in useGetTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx:29-53) has itemType, attributeType, project, substringMatch and the datetime fields, but no organization. Two organizations with the same page filters (e.g. no project selected, same period) share a cache entry, and the shared react-query cache can serve the other org's attribute keys until the refetch finishes. Add `organization.slug` to the key.

Switching to raw `useQuery` drops `retry: false` and changes what `isLoading` means

The previous `useApiQuery` call set `retry: false`, `staleTime: 0` and `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. The raw `useQuery` uses the client defaults (DEFAULT_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG in utils/queryClient.tsx:19-26 only turns off refetch on reconnect and on window focus), so retry is react-query's default of 3 with backoff. When `/trace-items/attributes/` fails, `isLoading` (now `isFetching`, line 61) stays true through the retries, so `TraceItemAttributeProvider` (contexts/traceItemAttributeContext.tsx:43-57) reports string and number attributes as loading for several seconds. It also reports loading on every background refetch, not just the first load without data. `attributes` can now be `undefined`; the provider's spreads tolerate that, but the return type changed. Consider `retry: false` and `isLoading` from the query result if the old behaviour was intended.

`height: 100%` dropped from the replaced FlexBox

The removed `FlexBox` had `flex-grow: 1; flex-direction: column; height: 100%`. `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>` sets `flex: 1 1 0%` and no height. If the parent is not a flex container, or relies on the child's `height: 100%`, the waterfall's height can change. Please confirm against the parent layout in the trace view.

TestGetCommentBody expects environment names but is not a Snuba test case

`test_simple` now expects ` in `dev`` / ` in `prod``. That text comes from `CommitContextIntegration.get_environment_info` (src/sentry/integrations/source_code_management/commit_context.py:584-597). It calls `issue.get_recommended_event()`, which queries Snuba (src/sentry/models/group.py:274, 870). `TestGetCommentBody` inherits only `GithubCommentTestCase` (an `IntegrationTestCase`), not `SnubaTestCase`. Only `SnubaTestCase.store_event` (src/sentry/testutils/cases.py:1058-1068) routes events into Snuba, so these events are probably never there. The lookup would return no event, or fail inside the swallowed `except Exception`, and the comment would have no ` in ...` suffix, so the assertion would fail. Make the class also inherit `SnubaTestCase`, as `TestTop5IssuesByCount` does a few lines above, or mock `get_environment_info`.

GitLab TestGetCommentBody has the same missing Snuba dependency for the environment suffix

The expected comment includes ` in `dev`` and ` in `prod``. These come from `get_environment_info`, which queries Snuba through `Group.get_recommended_event`. `TestGetCommentBody(GitlabCommentTestCase)` is not a `SnubaTestCase`, so `store_event` does not write to Snuba and the environment lookup most likely returns an empty string. Add `SnubaTestCase` to the class bases, or mock the lookup.

No test posts with `application/reports+json` any more

The old tests posted with `content_type="application/reports+json"`, the media type browsers send and the one `BrowserReportsJSONParser` handles (src/sentry/issues/endpoints/browser_reporting_collector.py:63-69, 82). The rewritten tests (`test_basic`, `test_handles_multiple_reports_both_specs`, and every validation test) all use the client's default format. The only test that sets a content type is the 415 one, which uses `bad/type/json`. Nothing now checks that the custom parser accepts the real content type. Pass `content_type="application/reports+json"` in at least `test_basic`. The assertion on the `browser_report_received` log call was also dropped, although the endpoint still logs it (line 93).

`Flex.Item grow={1}` is not equivalent to the removed `flex: 1`

The removed `FlexContainer` used `flex: 1`, which is `1 1 0%`. `Flex.Item grow={1}` renders `flex-grow:1; flex-shrink:1; flex-basis:auto` (static/app/components/core/layout/flex.tsx:35-46). With an auto basis, a long description or feature list gets a larger starting size, and the sibling `Metadata` block (line 362, a fixed-margin grid) shrinks in proportion. The previous layout kept `Metadata` at its natural width. `<Flex.Item flex="1">` reproduces the old behaviour exactly.

`division by zero` assertion can't tell title from message

The endpoint builds the log line as `'{title}: {message}'` (src/sentry/replays/endpoints/project_replay_summarize_breadcrumbs.py:126-131). `title` and `message` come from different nodestore keys (lines 114 and 116). For a ZeroDivisionError the stored title is normally already `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero`. So `assert any("division by zero" in log ...)` passes even if `message` comes back empty, and the test would not catch a bad `message` lookup. Assert the exact expected line instead, or build the event so `title` and `message` hold different strings. The test also never checks where the error line falls among the breadcrumbs. The ordering is only covered by the unit test at line 283.

No PUT test for omitting `owner` while one is already set

`update()` in src/sentry/workflow_engine/endpoints/validators/base/detector.py:66-79 has three branches: set the owner, clear it when `owner` is None, and do nothing when the key is absent (`"owner" in validated_data`). The new tests cover the first two. The third is not covered: every pre-existing PUT test sends `valid_data` without `owner` on a detector that has none. A regression that wipes the owner on any PUT without `owner` would pass the suite. Add a test that sets an owner, sends `valid_data` without `owner`, and asserts the owner is unchanged. The PUT path also has no test for an invalid owner or one from another organization. Only the POST tests (test_organization_detector_index.py:511-542) cover those.

OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot paginate the audit log's datetime key

The audit log endpoint orders by `-datetime` (`organization_auditlogs.py:80`), a DateTimeField. `get_item_key` here is copied from `Paginator` (integer keys): `math.floor(value)` on a `datetime` raises `TypeError`. `build_cursor` calls the key function on the first result (`utils/cursors.py:122`, `137`), so any non-empty page with `?optimized_pagination=true` returns a 500. `value_from_cursor` (line 843) also returns the raw cursor value. `DateTimePaginator` converts it back to a datetime (`paginator.py:238-241`). Here `build_queryset` would compare the `datetime` column to a millisecond integer. Queues are unbounded, so there is no backpressure despite the docstring

If workers are slower than the topic, e.g. a slow Redis/DB call, the consumer reads and decodes without limit. Memory grows with every queued `WorkItem`, which holds the whole `Message`. `OffsetTracker.all_offsets` and `outstanding` also grow. Shutdown flag stops workers before the queues are drained, contradicting `shutdown(immediate=False)`

Workers exit without draining items still in their queue, even though `immediate=False` implies a drain. Those offsets never complete, so they are not committed and are reprocessed after restart. close() has no overall bound and does not flush a final commit

`close()` joins the commit thread for up to 5s. `queue_pool.shutdown()` then joins each of the `num_queues` workers (default 20) with `timeout=5.0` in sequence (line 243). Worst case is about 5s + 20×5s = 105s if workers are blocked in slow processing. This runs inside Arroyo's revoke handler, so a stuck worker could block the rebalance for longer than the group's poll interval. Also, the commit thread is stopped before workers finish, so offsets completed during the drain are never committed. Use one shared deadline for all joins. Consider a final `get_committable_offsets()`/commit after workers stop.

`commit_function` is also called from the commit thread, not the consumer thread. Arroyo's commit callback and the underlying Kafka consumer are, as far as I know, not designed for cross-thread use. I could not check Arroyo here, so please confirm.

A single offset gap stalls commits for that partition permanently

Messages dropped by the decoder do go through `add_offset`/`complete_offset`, so they do not create gaps. Please confirm no other source of gaps exists. The bug is in `queue_consumer.py`, which belongs to the other part. This test should wait for at least two ticks (about 2.5s) and then assert that no commit exceeds 101. Shared BasePaginator now silently clamps negative offsets, and the comment misdescribes it

The read-lock fast path is released before `Lock()` is taken at line 48, and the cache is never re-checked after that. Async legacy writes inherit the request context and their errors are never logged

The legacy write runs in a goroutine, but its context is derived from the request `ctx` (`context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)`, also lines 110, 135 and 163). `Create`, `Delete`, `Update` and `DeleteCollection` return right after starting the goroutine. This matters more in mode 3 than in mode 1: mode 3 is meant to be the last step before legacy is retired, and the only trace of a failed legacy write is an error-labelled histogram sample. The old mode 3 wrapped the updated object in `updateWrapper` so legacy received the object storage had produced. Now legacy re-runs `objInfo.UpdatedObject` against its own copy of the old object, so the two stores can end up with different results, for example on resourceVersion or UID.
